description_en: The Satyanārāyaṇa temple lies to the south of the path reached after descending a flight of stairs to the east of the raised platform bearing the Aṃśuvarmā inscription in Hãḍīgāũ. This location is geographically the lowest point of Hãḍīgāũ (S. Tivārī 2023, p. 22). The place referred to as “Dvalakānimam” in theGopālarājavaṃśāvalī(Vajrācārya and Malla 1985, folio 21B-22A) is identified as the site of the Satyanārāyaṇa temple (S. Tivārī 2023, p. 91), and the deity mentioned as “Tilapāla Viṣṇu Bhaṭṭāraka” (protector of the sesame seed) is the Viṣṇu statue enshrined within the temple's sanctum (Slusser 1982, Vol. 1, p. 247).The west-facing temple features a dome with a goldenkalaśaatop it and additionalkalaśas at its corners. Below, a metal-roofed section covers the temple. The sanctum lacks atoraṇaabove the entrance. Inside, a west-facing Viṣṇu statue of stone stands on ajalaharībase, enshrined as the temple's main deity. Worshipped as Satyanārāyaṇa, Viṣṇu's upper right hand appears to hold a discus (cakra). Though broken, the upper left hand likely held a mace (gadā). The lower right hand displays the boon-granting gesture (varadamudrā) while holding a lotus seed (padmavīja). The lower left carries a conch shell (śaṅkha). Regmī (VS 2030, p. 130) suggests this statue might depict Vedavyāsa instead of Viṣṇu. A copper repoussé rendering of Viṣṇu covers the old Viṣṇu statue. Other statues and ajalaharīare also within the sanctum.A Garuḍa column stands before the temple. Anuparama Gupta, a prominent figure in the Licchavi administration, erected this column in honor of Dvaipāyana Vyāsa. Atop the column is the Garuḍa statue exhibiting the gesture of reverence (namaskāramudrā). A human-like Garuḍa statues are customarily erected in front of Viṣṇu statues in Nepal. These statues often resemble the face of the devotee sponsoring the statue (G. Vajrācārya VS 2033, p. 127). Possibly, Anuparama Gupta established this statue to reflect his own likeness (Slusser 2005, p. 43). A Paśupati temple with a four-facedśivaliṅgainside stands southeast of the temple. The wall south of the temple displays ancient statues.No explicit records have been found regarding the construction of this temple or the installation of the Viṣṇu statue within. However, the artifacts in the temple suggest that the temple’s origin goes back to the Licchavi period. While some scholars (Bangdel 1995, p. 116) have dated the Viṣṇu statue within the sanctum to the 2nd-3rd century CE, others (Schroeder 2019, p. 404) have placed it in the 4th century CE.Anuparama Gupta, a powerful figure during the Licchavi period, erected a Garuḍa column in front of the temple and inscribed verses dedicated to Dvaipāyana Vyāsa. Anuparama Gupta's wife was Ābhirī Gominī, and his son was Bhauma Gupta, who later became a powerful figure in the Licchavi administration. This inscription, with its mature writing style and philosophical content, is considered of high quality. While the inscription lacks a specific date or the name of the reigning king, based on its script, it is attributed to the reign of Vasantadeva, who succeeded Mānadeva (D. Vajrācārya VS 2030, pp. 158). As Anuparama Gupta's wife, Ābhirī Gominī, installed the Anuparameśvara Śivaliṅga at Paśupati in 540 CE (ŚS 462) (D. Vajrācārya VS 2030, pp. 170-171), it can be inferred that Anuparama Gupta died around that time. Therefore, the Garuḍa column in front of the Satyanārāyaṇa temple must predate 540 CE. Although some scholars (Slusser 1982, Vol. 2, plate 381) suggest that Anuparama Gupta himself installed the Viṣṇu statue around the mid-6th century CE, a definitive conclusion cannot be reached without more concrete evidence.TheGopālarājavaṃśāvalīstates that King Jīva Gupta gilded the roof of the Tilapāla Viṣṇu Bhaṭṭāraka temple (Vajrācārya and Malla 1985, folio 21B-22A). While no king named Jīva Gupta is found in Nepali history, it was Jiṣṇu Gupta, a powerful figure who issued his own coins, was referred to as Jīva Gupta in the chronicle (J. Regmī VS 2053, p. 153, 167). Anuparama Gupta, who erected a stone pillar with a eulogy to Dvaipāyana Vyāsa in front of the temple, was Jiṣṇu Gupta's great-grandfather. After consolidating his power, Jiṣṇu Gupta possibly renovated the temple and gilded its roof.The artifacts at the temple premises also support the temple's antiquity. The Kubera statue (KAT3080-021) in the temple courtyard is dated to the 4th century (Bangdel 1982, p. 164, plate 76), while the Cāmuṇḍā statue (KAT3080-018) is said to belong to the 6th-7th century (Slusser 1982, Vol. 2, plate 561). The oldest inscription found within the temple's sanctum dates to 1545 CE (NS 665). This inscription records the installation of an Umāmaheśvara statue by Kesarāma, Jayakīta Bhāro, Bhārasiṃṅa Bhāro, and others during the reign of King Narendra Malla. The Umāmaheśvara statue is now lost, with only thejalaharī(KAT3080-002) remaining.To delve deeper into the antiquity of the temple site, Italian archaeologists conducted excavations to the west and south of the temple courtyard in the 1980s. These excavations unearthed the remnants of brick structures dating back to the 2nd century BCE, predating the Lichhavi period (S. Tivārī 2023, p. 97). Additionally, a datedjaḥdhuṃwater tank was discovered. The inscription on thejaḥdhuṃstates that Priyavarmana installed the water tank at Andigrāma on the 5th of the bright fortnight of Vaiśākha in 750 CE (Mānadeva Era 174) (D. Vajrācārya VS 2053, p. 600-iii). The inscription confirms that the current name of Hā̃ḍīgāũ originated from Andigrāma.In 2021 CE, Durham University in the UK, in partnership with the Department of Archaeology, conducted a Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) survey primarily focusing on the western and southern areas within the temple courtyard. The GPR survey revealed buried heaps of stone and brick. These remains could be the scattered remnants of walls collapsed in an earthquake. The survey suggested that further archaeological excavations should be undertaken to explore the possibility of an ancient urban settlement within the temple complex (Coningham et al. 2021, p. 30).The priestly duties at this temple are performed by a local Śreṣṭha caste member. He conducts daily morning prayers and eveningāratīrituals, offering devotion with lamps. Without any formal remuneration, the offerings made by the devotees form the primary source of his income.In honor of Satyanārāyaṇa, a unique palanquin procession of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara is organized annually on the 1st of the dark fortnight of Kārtika. Also known as the Cokṭe Nārāyaṇa Jātrā, the procession features inverted palanquins carrying the deities on top, with the finial placed below. Wax flowers are used during the procession. Due to this distinctive characteristic, the procession is locally referred to as the “thejātrāof Hā̃ḍīgāũ that does not exist elsewhere."
description_ne: हाँडीगाउँमा अंशुवर्माको शिलालेख रहेको डबलीबाट पूर्वपट्टि सिँढीबाट तल झरेपछि बाटोको दक्षिणमा सत्यनारायण मन्दिर रहेको छ । जुन स्थनमा यो मन्दिर रहेको छ, त्यो स्थान भौगोलिक रूपले हाँडीगाउँको सबभन्दा तल्लो स्थान हो (S. Tivārī 2023, p. 22) ।गोपालराजवंशावली(Vajrācārya and Malla 1985, folio 21B-22A) मा 'द्वलकानिमम्' भनिएको ठाउँ सत्यनारायण मन्दिर रहेको ठाउँ हो (S. Tivārī 2023, p. 91) र 'तिलपाल विष्णुभट्टारक' (protector of the sesame seed) भनी उल्लेख गरिएका देवता मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र रहेको विष्णुमूर्ति हो (Slusser 1982, Vol. 1, p. 247) । पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी बनाइएको यो मन्दिर गुम्बज शैलीमा बनाइएको छ । सुवर्ण कलशलाई गजूरको रूपमा राखिएको यस मन्दिरको गुम्बजको चारै कुनामा पनि गजूर राखिएका छन् । गुम्बजभन्दा तल्लो भागमा धातुको पाता राखिएको छाना पनि रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामाथि तोरण राखिएको छैन । गर्भगृहभित्र मन्दिरको मुख्य देवताको रूपमा जलहरिमाथि पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी विष्णुको ढुङ्गाको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । उनै विष्णुलाई सत्यनारायण भनी पूजा गरिन्छ । विष्णुका चार हातमध्ये माथिल्लो दायाँ हातले चक्र लिएको जस्तो देखिन्छ । माथिल्लो बायाँ हात भाँचिएको छ, तर त्यहाँ गदा धारण गरेको हुनुपर्छ । तल्लो दायाँ हात पद्मवीजसहतिको वरद मुद्रामा छ भने तल्लो बायाँ हातमा शङ्ख छ । Regmī (VS 2030, p. 130) ले यस मूर्तिलाई विष्णुको नभई वेदव्यासको हुनसक्ने अनुमान गरेका छन् । विष्णुको पुरानो मूर्तिलाई तामाको repousse मूर्तिले छोपेर राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र अन्य केही मूर्तिसहित जलहरि पनि स्थापना गरिएको छ । मन्दिरअगाडि प्रस्तस्तम्भमाथि गरुड स्तम्भ ठड्याइएको छ । लिच्छविकालका एक प्रभावशाली व्यक्ति अनुपरम गुप्तले द्वैपायन व्यासको प्रसंशा गरी ठड्याएको स्तम्भमाथि नमस्कार मुद्रामा गरूडको प्रतिमा राखिएको छ । नेपालमा विष्णुको मूर्ति स्थापना गर्दा त्यस मूर्तिको अगाडि गरूडको मनुष्याकार मूर्ति स्थापना गर्ने चलन छ । गरूडको त्यस्तो मूर्ति प्रायः विष्णु मूति स्थापना गर्ने भक्तजनको अनुहारसँग मिल्ने गरी बनाइन्छ (G. Vajrācārya VS 2033, p. 127) । त्यसैले अनुपरम गुप्तले आफ्नै अनुहार झल्कने गरी गरूड स्तम्भमाथि उक्त प्रतिमा राखेको हुनसक्छ (Slusser 2005, p. 43) । मन्दिरको दक्षिण-पूर्वमा चतुर्मुखी शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरिएको पशुपति मन्दिर रहेको छ भने दक्षिणतर्फको भित्तामा पुराना मूर्तिहरू राखिएका छन् ।यो मन्दिर र मन्दिरभित्रको विष्णुको स्थापनाबारे स्पष्ट अभिलेख पाइएको छैन । अभिलेख नभएपनि मन्दिरमा पाइएका कलाकृतिको आधारमा लिच्छविकालमा नै यो मन्दिर अस्तित्वमा आइसकेको देखिन्छ । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र रहेको विष्णुको मूर्तिलाई कसैले ईशाको दोस्रो-तेस्रो शताब्दीको मानेका छन् (Bangdel 1995, p. 116) भने कसैले ईशाको चौथौ शताब्दीको मानेका छन् (Schroeder 2019, p. 404) । लिच्छविकालका एक शक्तिशाली व्यक्ति अनुपरम गुप्तले मन्दिर अगाडि गरूड स्तम्भ खडा गरी द्वैपायन व्यासको स्तोत्र लेखेर कुँदाएका थिए । उनले बौद्धहरूलाई नास्तिक र कुतार्किक भनी खण्डन गरेका छन् र वैदिक धर्मलाई पुनः प्रतिष्ठापन गर्ने व्यक्तित्वको रूपमा द्वैपायन व्यासको प्रसंशा गरेका छन् । यी अनुपरम गुप्तकी श्रीमती आभिरी गोमिनी र छोरा भौम गुप्त थिए । भौम गुप्त पछि गएर लिच्छवि शासन व्यवस्थामा शक्तिशाली व्यक्तिका रूपमा देखापरेका थिए । प्रौढ लेखनशैली, दार्शनिक विचारधारा आदिको दृष्टिले यो अभिलेख उच्चकोटीको मानिएको छ । यो अभिलेखमा तिथिमिति नलेखिएको र तात्कालिक राजाको नाम पनि लेखिएको छैन । तैपनि लिपिको आधारमा यो अभिलेखलाई मानदेवपछिका वसन्तदेवको पालाको मानिएको छ (D. Vajrācārya VS 2030, pp. 158) । शसं ४६२ (सन् ५४०) मा अनुपरम गुप्तकी श्रीमती आभिरी गोमिनीले पशुपतिमा अनुपरमेश्वर शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरेकीले (D. Vajrācārya VS 2030, pp. 170-171) उक्त मितिमा अनुपरम गुप्तको मृत्यु भएको हुनुपर्छ । त्यसैले सत्यनारायण मन्दिरअगाडि रहेको गरूड स्तम्भ सन् ५४० भन्दा अघिको हुनुपर्ने देखिन्छ । अनुपरम गुप्तले नै ईशाको छैठौं शताब्दीको मध्यतिर विष्णुको मूर्ति पनि स्थापना गरेको (Slusser 1982, Vol. 2, plate 381) भनिएपनि ठोस प्रमाण प्राप्त नभएसम्म किटेर भन्न सकिने अवस्था छैन ।गोपालराजवंशावलीमा राजा जीव गुप्तले तिलपाल विष्णुभट्टारकलाई सुनको छाना हाले भनी लेखिएको छ (Vajrācārya and Malla 1985, folio 21B-22A) । नेपालको इतिहासमा जीव गुप्त नाम गरेका कुनै राजा छैनन् तर राजाभन्दा शक्तिशाली भएर आफ्नै नाममा मुद्रा निकाल्ने जिष्णु गुप्तलाई वंशावलीमा जीव गुप्त भनिएको हो (J. Regmī VS 2053, p. 153, 167) । मन्दिरअगाडि द्वैपायन व्यासको स्तोत्र लेखेर शिलास्तम्भ खडा गर्ने अनुपरम गुप्त उनका जुजुबाजे थिए । जिष्णु गुप्तले आफू शक्तिशाली भएपछि मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरी सुनको छाना हालेको हुनसक्छ । मन्दिर प्राङ्गणमा रहेका कलाकृतिहरूले पनि मन्दिरको प्राचीनता पुष्टि गर्न सहयोग गर्छन् । मन्दिर प्राङ्गणमा रहेको कुबेर (KAT3080-021) को मूर्तिलाई ईशाको चौथौ शताब्दीको मानिएको छ (Bangdel 1982, p. 164, plate 76) भने चामुण्डा (KAT3080-018) लाई ईशाको छैठौं-सातौं शताब्दीको मूर्ति मानिएको छ (Slusser 1982, Vol. 2, plate 561) । मन्दिरको गर्भगृहभित्र रहेको सबैभन्दा पुरानो अभिलेख नेसं ६६५ (सन् १५४५) को हो । उक्त अभिलेखमा राजा नरेन्द्र मल्लको राज्यकालमा केसराम, जयकीत भारो, भारसिंङ भारो लगायतका व्यक्तिहरूले मिलेर उमामहेश्वरको प्रतिमा स्थापना गरेको कुरा लेखिएको छ । अहिले उमामहेश्वरको मूर्ति हराइसकेको छ, जलहरि (KAT3080-002) मात्र बाँकी छ ।मन्दिर रहेको स्थानको प्राचीनताबारे थप खोजी गर्न सन् ८० को दशकमा इटालियन पुरातत्त्वविद्‌हरूले मन्दिर प्राङ्गणभन्दा बाहिर पश्चिम र दक्षिणतर्फ उत्खनन गरेको थियो । उक्त उत्खननमा इँटाबाट निर्मित लिच्छविकालभन्दा अगाडि ईपू दोस्रो शताब्दीतिरका संरचनाहरूको अवशेष भेटिएका थिए (S. Tivārī 2023, p. 97) । उत्खननमा एउटा जलद्रोणी पनि भेटिएको थियो । त्यस जलद्रोणीमा अन्दिग्राममा मासं १७४ (सन् ७५०) वैशाख शुक्ल ५ को दिनमा प्रियवर्मनले जलद्रोणी राखेको कुरा लेखिएको छ (D. Vajrācārya VS 2053, p. 600-iii) । उक्त अभिलेख भेटिएपछि अन्दिग्रामबाट वर्तनाममा प्रयोग भइरहेको नाम हाँडीगाउँ विकास भएको पुष्टि भएको छ । सन् २०२१ मा बेलायतको दुरहम विश्वविद्यालयले पुरातत्त्व विभागसँग मिलेर Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) सर्वेक्षण गरेको थियो । मन्दिर प्राङ्गणभित्रै पश्चिम र दक्षिणपट्टिको क्षेत्रमा केन्द्रित उक्त सर्वेक्षणले जमीनमुनि ढुङ्गा र इँटाको थुप्रो दबिएर रहेको देखाएको थियो । ती अवशेषहरू भूकम्पले गारो भत्किँदा छरिएका हुनसक्छन् । उक्त सर्वेक्षणले मन्दिर परिसरमा प्राचीन नगरबस्तीको अवशेष भेट्टिन सक्ने हुनाले पुरातात्त्विक उत्खनन गरेर हेर्नुपर्ने सुझाव दिएको थियो (Coningham et al 2021, p. 30) ।यस मन्दिरमा श्रेष्ठ थरका व्यक्तिले पूजारीको काम गरिरहेका छन् । उनले बिहान नित्यपूजा गरी बेलुकी आरती दिने काम गरिरहेका छन् । उनलाई गुठी संस्थान वा अन्य कुनै निकायबाट पारिश्रमिकको व्यवस्था गरिएको छैन । भक्तजनहरूले चढाउने भेटी नै उनको आन्दानीको स्रोत बनेको छ । सत्यनारायणको सम्मानमा प्रत्येक वर्ष कार्तिक कृष्ण प्रतिपदाको दिनमा ब्रह्मा, विष्णु, महेश्वरलाई खटमा राखी जात्रा गरिन्छ । यस जात्रालाई चोक्टे नारायण जात्रा पनि भनिन्छ । यस जात्रामा खटको गजूर उल्टाइने, देउतालाई गजूरभन्दा माथि राखिने र मैनको फूल प्रयोग गरिन्छ । यस्तो प्रचलन कुनै पनि जात्रामा नहुने भएकाले यो जात्रालाई ‘कहीँ नभएको जात्रा हाँडीगाउँको’ भनिएको हो ।

historical_events.event_description: Anuparama Gupta, a powerful figure during the Licchavi period, erected a Garuḍa column in front of the temple and inscribed verses dedicated to Dvaipāyana Vyāsa. Anuparama Gupta's wife was Ābhirī Gominī, and his son was Bhauma Gupta, who later became a powerful figure in the Licchavi administration. This inscription, with its mature writing style and philosophical content, is considered of high quality. While the inscription lacks a specific date or the name of the reigning king, based on its script, it is attributed to the reign of Vasantadeva, who succeeded Mānadeva. A human-like Garuḍa statues are customarily erected in front of Viṣṇu statues in Nepal. These statues often resemble the face of the devotee sponsoring the statue (G. Vajrācārya VS 2033, p. 127). Possibly, Anuparama Gupta established this statue to reflect his own likeness. As Anuparama Gupta's wife, Ābhirī Gominī, installed the Anuparameśvara Śivaliṅga at Paśupati in 540 CE (ŚS 462) (D. Vajrācārya VS 2030, pp. 170-171), it can be inferred that Anuparama Gupta died around that time. Therefore, the Garuḍa column in front of the Satyanārāyaṇa temple must predate 540 CE (cp. Acharya 2007, pp. 30-32).

During the reign of King Narendra Malla, Kesarāma, Jayakīta Bhāro, Bhārasiṃṅa Bhāro, and others installed an Umāmaheśvara statue, which is now lost, with only thejalaharī(KAT3080-002) remaining in the southeastern corner of the sanctum.

This inscription does not seem to be related to the Satyanārāyaṇa temple and was probably brought from elsewhere to be placed within the temple. The inscription mentions that Muni Thakuṃ and Dhanamāyā Śreṣṭha constructed aphalcāon the road leading from the east to the west of Hā̃ḍīgāũ. Due topotātax imposed on the tworopanīs of land allocated for thephalcā, they donated it to a trust. The trust members performed fire oblations in front of thephalcāonce a year and offered refreshments to travelers.
Statues of Jhanakumārī and Divyakumārī were installed. The name of the donor is not mentioned.

historical_events.event_name: Repair of the Paśupati Mahādeva Temple (KAT3080-008)
historical_events.event_description: With the joint assistance from Mahendranātha Upādhyāya and Aṣṭabahādura Prajāpatī, the Paśupati Mahādeva temple (KAT3080-008) southeast of Satyanārāyaṇa was renovated.
Along with their sons, Bhaktabahādura Śreṣṭha and Ciraṇadevī Śreṣṭha offered an oblong banner (patāḥ) to the temple.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of a metal statue of Nārāyaṇa
historical_events.event_description: In memory of his late father Buddhimāna Maharjana and mother Nānīcā Maharjana, Pañcanārāyaṇa Maharjana, along with his family members from Hā̃ḍīgāũ, offered a full-sized copper statue of Nārāyaṇa to cover the original Lichhavi-era statue.

Durham University in the UK, in partnership with the Department of Archaeology, conducted a Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) survey primarily focusing on the western and southern areas within the temple courtyard. The GPR survey revealed buried heaps of stone and brick. These remains could be the scattered remnants of walls collapsed in an earthquake. The survey suggested that further archaeological excavations should be undertaken to explore the possibility of an ancient urban settlement within the temple complex.
